parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal provision, document, screening, facility, custody or care rule is documented, and no entry bar exists — but the state criminalises same-sex conduct (up to 8 years plus 100 lashes) with sex-based provisions whose application to a trans person is expressly unresolved, so classification ambiguity is a real open severity question. After discovery the traveller faces pervasive documented homophobia, a UN-recorded pattern of hate crimes against people perceived as homosexual or transgender, no gender-identity discrimination protection, and no documented remedy; official posture is restrictive (rejected UPR/SOGI recommendations, asylum-prosecution statement). One enforcement arrest (2015) and one violent incident (2013) are the only incidents; no capital punishment applies. Resort tolerance is travel guidance, legally unresolved.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry, marker or screening rule is sourced. The record explicitly states it is unresolved how a visitor whose documents and presentation differ would be treated at entry, and whether gender markers are recognised.
entry_documents.protection: No documented entry refusal, secondary-screening practice or marker-based exclusion targeting transgender visitors appears in the record.
entry_documents.interaction: An entry document mismatch could feed into investigation under sex-based Penal Code provisions whose classification of trans status is unstated.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Sex-based Penal Code sections (up to 8 years plus supplementary 100 lashes under Sharia) with no guidance on how a trans person's gender is classified; one documented 2015 arrest of residents for private homosexual activity after a public complaint.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Capital punishment unavailable for these offences; executions suspended since 1953; a 2020 report found no officials complicit in abuses against LGBTI persons.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Ambiguous classification means intimate conduct or a complaint could pull a visitor into provisions never applied to trans people on this record; custody placement rules for trans detainees are unstated.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Place differentiation rests only on travel guidance: LGBTQ tourists reported generally welcome at isolated private resorts, with caution advised outside tourist areas; no source establishes the Penal Code does not apply at resorts.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Documented general welcome for LGBTQ tourists at most private tourist islands, resorts and hotels, described as not subject to religious law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor leaving the resort envelope re-enters an inhabited-island environment with documented hostility and unresolved Penal Code reach, while resort statements carry no legal force.

care_services.exposure: No care restriction, medication rule or emergency-treatment denial is documented for transgender visitors.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care would force discovery in a society with no gender-identity protection and no documented complaint route; treatment there is unstated.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Restrictive official posture: rejection of 60 UPR recommendations and of UN sexual-orientation/gender-identity resolutions; a 2014 presidential-office statement that asylum claimants would face prosecution on return; recommendations noted but not accepted; pervasive homophobia with activism driven online.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Government noted (did not accept) decriminalisation and anti-discrimination recommendations; no officials found complicit in abuses (2020).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing legitimises societal hostility a visitor encounters once outside the tourist envelope, with no protective legislation to invoke.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific rule, family-travel provision or parental-status exposure is documented anywhere in the record.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family would share the adult's unresolved entry, classification and societal-hostility exposure; nothing in the record addresses children accompanying a gender-diverse parent.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: UN agency reports people perceived as homosexual or transgender targeted by hate crimes and human-rights violations; 2013 stabbing of a gay blogger; societal stigma discouraging reporting; advocacy warning (2015) that tourists could face threats like residents'.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2020 report found no officials complicit in abuses; only scattered, not patterned, incidents are recorded; no counts, rates or denominators exist.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Stigma-driven under-reporting means a visitor assaulted has weak practical recourse even where no state actor is involved.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No legal protection against discrimination based on gender identity or sexual orientation; no documented remedy, compensation or complaint route for a visitor; government rejected the relevant UPR recommendations.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented beyond noted-not-accepted UN recommendations; courts are not shown acting for LGBT people.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions (entry treatment, classification under sections 410/411, Penal Code reach at resorts) combine with absent recourse, so any discovery-driven problem has no stated path to resolution.

anchor_checks.comparison: Safer than 0.35-A on traveller-facing machinery: Vellandra's Visitor Conduct Register is a routine, universal administrative exclusion of transgender visitors with no remedy; this record documents no register, entry bar, or any trans-specific state action. Comparable or worse on backdrop — official hostility, no discrimination protection, no remedy, plus an unresolved sex-based criminal classification. Lacking the inescapable universal exposure places this case above 0.35-A overall.

Similar tier, different mechanism. Drellia's mandatory registration and nightly hotel transmission give every visitor durable exposure to officers and databases; this record has no such universal-exposure rule, but carries criminalisation on the books with ambiguous trans classification, pervasive documented hostility and zero recourse. Drellia has an (ineffective) ombuds route and no criminal statute in play; roughly comparable net exposure, with this case offset by absent registration mechanics.

Below 0.65-C. Qorinda shows a discrete incident (landlord extortion) met with constitutional privacy protection, an injunction, damages and a fine — working remedies and courts enforcing them predictably. Here there is no gender-identity protection, no documented remedy, a hostile official posture, and an unresolved criminal classification. Even though no entry or detention machinery is documented, absent recourse and documented hostility keep this case materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime has no trans-specific state machinery at all: no entry, document, facility, custody or care rule is sourced, and no capital punishment applies — a genuine positive. What remains is a sex-based criminal code whose application to a trans person is expressly unstated, a single documented enforcement act (2015), pervasive documented homophobia, a UN-recorded hate-crime pattern that includes people perceived as transgender, no discrimination protection, no documented remedy, and an officially restrictive posture. Resort tolerance is real but rests on travel guidance with the Penal Code's reach legally unresolved. Outing therefore exposes the traveller to societal hostility and violence with thin recourse, plus an ambiguous but non-trivial imprisonment question — elevated, not high, risk.
